summary.text: Oceanic crust is the uppermost layer of the ocean parts of tectonic plates, made mainly of mafic rock rich in iron and magnesium.
It is thinner than continental crust but denser, about 3.0 grams per cubic centimeter against roughly 2.7, and it is continuously created at mid-ocean ridges.
Subduction consumes older oceanic lithosphere, so oceanic crust is seldom more than 200 million years old.

facts.label: Typical thickness
facts.value: About 7 km, give or take 1 km

facts.label: Biggest layer
facts.value: Layer 3 gabbro, over two-thirds of the volume

facts.label: Iceland's crust
facts.value: About 20 km thick, above a plume

items.prompt: A research ship samples seafloor rock at points farther and farther from a mid-ocean ridge. How does the age of the rock change?
items.explain: The youngest oceanic rocks are at the ridges, and they get progressively older away from them.

items.prompt: Where an oceanic plate meets a continental plate at a convergent boundary, which one sinks into the mantle?

options.label: The oceanic one, since continental is less dense
The continental one, since it is thicker
Neither, both pile up into mountains

items.explain: The oceanic lithosphere always subducts in this case because the continental lithosphere is less dense.

items.prompt: The mantle under Iceland is hotter than usual. How does that affect the oceanic crust formed there?

options.label: It is the same as anywhere else
No crust forms there at all

items.explain: Hotter mantle starts melting deeper, making more melt and thicker crust; Iceland's crust is about 20 km thick.

items.prompt: At a ridge that spreads very slowly, rising mantle has time to cool on the way up. What kind of crust results?
items.explain: Cooler rising mantle melts at a shallower depth, producing less melt and crust only 4–5 km thick.

items.prompt: Compare the layer of sediment on the seafloor right at a mid-ocean ridge with the layer far away from it. What would you find?

options.label: Thin or missing near the ridge, thicker far away
Missing everywhere on the ocean floor

items.explain: Sediment is usually thin or absent near ridges and thicker farther away, as it builds up on rock moving away from the ridge.

items.prompt: Most oceanic crust around the world is close to the same thickness. What explains this?

options.label: Ocean water presses it to a set thickness
Sediment fills it up to a fixed level
Erosion trims it down evenly over time
Melt amount depends only on mantle temperature

items.explain: The amount of melt depends only on the rising mantle's temperature, so most oceanic crust ends up about 7 km thick.
